title: One, Peak, Life, and the Upgrade
lessons: The player reaches WHOOP through a comparison of One, Peak, and Life rather than a simple hardware price.
The player already owns older WHOOP hardware and is offered a newer device by extending membership or paying an upgrade fee.

text: Cafe, laptop, the WHOOP page. There's no price for the band. There's a table: One, Peak, Life.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why are there three relationship levels before I even put the band on?

entry-first-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Because you're not buying the band. You're buying how much of me you get to hear from.

entry-first-4.speaker: WHOOP
text: One: the basics. Sleep, strain, recovery. Peak: stress, Healthspan, the deeper reads. Life: the medical-grade band, ECG, heart stuff. Three doors, same house.

choice-first.speaker: WHOOP
text: Your coffee's getting cold and you're still on the table. Which door?

choices.text: I like being able to choose how deep this goes.
This makes a wearable feel like software pricing.
I want to buy a device once and own the features.

first-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Then pick the smallest one that answers a question you actually have. Don't buy Life because it sounds serious. Buy it because your heart is the question.

first-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: It is software pricing. The band and the membership are one thing. I'd rather you see that on the page than find it on the invoice.

first-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: Then I'm structurally not your favorite product model.
An email: your band is a generation old. There's a newer one, and two ways to get it.

entry-return-5.speaker: WHOOP
text: Extend your membership and the new band comes with it. Or pay a one-time fee for the band and keep your membership dates where they are.

choice-return.speaker: WHOOP
text: Neither is free. I'd rather you know that before you pick.

choices.text: I like a way to upgrade without throwing away the membership time.
You're still asking me to spend more to stay current.
I don't want hardware upgrades tied to membership decisions.

return-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Good. I didn't want the time you already paid for to disappear because a sensor got better.

return-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Yes. New hardware is an upsell. It's a good upsell. It's still an upsell, and you're right to say it to my face.

return-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: That's the model. I can explain it more clearly. I can't make it something you buy once. I've tried to imagine it. It isn't me.
